observations: Three rounded forms outlined in thick black strokes sit side by side, with looping lines suggesting circular eyes, ears, and tooth-filled mouths across the lower half.
A dense underlayer of orange, teal, blue, red, and pink scratchy lines fills the background, visible through and around the black outlines like a tangled web.
Bold white scrawled marks cut across the middle zone, overlapping the black forms and creating a loose scribble layer that partially obscures the shapes beneath.
reading: Three black-outlined heads crowd the frame shoulder to shoulder, their features reduced to loops and open curves. Behind them, a hot orange-and-purple field of tangled lines pulses through every gap. The white scrawl layered across their faces reads as interruption—obscuring mouths and eyes, lending the group a feeling of being spoken over or half-erased. The composition can feel both communal and chaotic, figures jostling for visibility.
contextAngle: Scrimshaw3 sits between "Scrimshaw2" and "Scrimshaw4" in the owned numbered family. Where "Scrimshaw2" centers a single blue-and-teal form, this work multiplies figures to three and shifts to warm orange and purple, marking a clear change in density and palette within the owned subset.

connections.reason: "Scrimshaw2" uses a single looping head in cool blues and greens, making the jump to three warm-toned heads here a visible shift in crowding and color temperature.
Both layer bright scratchy color beneath heavy black outlines defining face-like shapes, though the nnxyz piece uses darker fill while Scrimshaw3 lets the background blaze through.

lookingQuestion: How does the white scrawl across the three faces change your sense of whether these figures are distinct individuals or merging into one another?
ambiguities: Whether the white marks represent text, signatures, or purely abstract scribble cannot be confirmed from the image alone.
The number of distinct figures could be read as two or three depending on how overlapping outlines at center are parsed.
